sentences.text:
The instant cr. misc. petition has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceedings including the order taking cognizance dated 24.02.2015 passed by learned Special Judge, CBI-cum-District Judge-I, Dhanbad in RC Case No. 16(A) of 2012-D, whereby and whereunder, prima facie case has been found to be made out under Sections 201, 423, 424, 467, 468, 471, 420 of Indian Penal Code and Section 13 (2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
2.

The case in brief relates to dishonest and fraudulent sale/ transfer of non- transferable raiyat land and Government land (Gauchar, Anabad, Rasta, Bandh, Ahra etc.) to different purchasers, and in the process of above illegal and unauthorized transfer of land, record of rights (khatiyan) and other land related records were manipulated/ created, substituted in records, obtained certified true copies thereof, claimed ownership and obtained bogus favourable Bhu Satyapan certificate/ No Objection Certificate with connivance of government officials and non-transferable land/
government land were shown as transferable (Basauri) in those bogus records and were sold to various purchasers.

3. In this manner, the land measuring 505.08 acres of total 363 land plots situated in 8 villages/mouzas under Mohanpur Circle, District Deoghar, Jharkhand was transferred by 25 registered sale deeds during 2009-11.

Out of 25 sale certificates, the original related sale certificate registers and corresponding original Index-II register for the period 1936-38 and other important Umakant Jha vs State Of Jharkhand Through The C.B.I. ... on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84138238/
1 land records were kept in District Record Room, Deoghar which was allegedly stolen in August, 2011 regarding which a separate FIR vide 260 / 2011 was registered by Deoghar Town Police Station in which Sunil Poddar and Dhrub Narayan Parihast were convicted by the court of Judicial Magistrate,
Deoghar.

sentences.text:
4. There was wide scale forgery in 25 sale certificates of the year 1936 - 38 by substituting forged sale certificates nature of land was changed from non- transferable to transferable.
5. Modus operandi was by replacing original sale certificate available in the District Record Room,
Dumka with fake and forged ones by manipulating the original Khatiyan of the District Record Room, Deoghar.
In this way, false No Objection Certificates were issued on the basis of forged sale certificates 6.
The present petitioner dishonestly executed the sale deed for non- transferable land on the basis of power of attorney land issued to him in criminal conspiracy with accused Dhrub Narayan Parihast.
CASE OF THE PETITIONER 7.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was not named in the FIR and he was the power of attorney holder of raiyat Sukri Raiyan who executed power of attorney in favour of the petitioner on 12.10.2010.
On the strength of the power of attorney he executed different sale deeds to the purchasers which has been detailed in the charge sheet.

8. It is submitted that no role has been attributed to the petitioner in issuance of any No Objection Certificate with respect to the land regarding which power of attorney was executed in his favour.

Further, there is no material to show or any allegation is made that the petitioner was involved in the manipulation of the records or the sale certificates which were substituted in the record room.
The petitioner had prima facie satisfaction from the No Objection Certificate and the sale certificates executed in favour of the vendors took the power of attorney and disposed of the land as per the instruction of the principal vendor.
Although it is alleged that there was an element of criminal conspiracy in executing the sale deed, but there is no material on the basis of which the imputation of conspiracy has been made.
There is no material to show that the petitioner had entered into criminal conspiracy with accused Drub Narayan Parihast.
9. Principal and original owner of the land Sukri Raiyan has not raised any objection to the sale executed by the petitioner.
Civil remedy for cancellation of sale deed in contravention to the provision of the SPT Act, were available under Section 20 and 42 of the Santhal Pargana Tenancy Act, 1949.
It is also submitted charge sheet was not submitted against the principal donor of the power of attorney, however, the court took cognizance.

2 10.

Learned Addl. Solicitor General of India, appearing for the CBI, has contested the quashing petition and submitted that Sukri Raiyan was a poor old lady and in a physically weak frame of body and it has come in her statement that she had not executed any deed of conveyance and power of attorney in favour of anybody.
Her thumb impression was taken by co-accused Drub Narayan Parihast.
It is further submitted that these are the disputed question of fact which can be addressed only at the stage of trial as to whether power of attorney was executed duly by her or not.
This is an issue which cannot be considered at this stage.
ANALYSIS 11.

Prosecution case unfolds a grim commentary of resources of land grabbers, who can hack the system to bypass law by getting access to even the district record rooms, forging documents,
projecting the land as transferable, manage no objection certificate and transferring land which are non-transferable as per law.

12. Santhal Pargana Tenancy Act, 1949 creates transferable and non- transferable categories of land,
under which only the land which are recorded in the record of rights can be transferred.
13. It is not disputed that non-transferable lands were sold by this petitioner on the strength of power of attorney executed by Sukri Raiyan.
Petitioner claims that he was ignorant about the earlier manipulations in the land records by multifarious contrivances.

It is contended on behalf of the CBI that the Donor Sukri Raiyan has in her statement during investigation stated that her thumb impressions were taken on blank sheet of papers by Dhrub Narayan Parihast, who has been convicted in a related case for theft and forgery of revenue records.

Petitioner claims to have executed the sale deed on the basis of power of attorney holder, who on her part states that she put her thumb impression on the document concerned as asked by Dhrub Narayan Paihast.

14. Without entering into probative value of the evidence collected, it is apparent that the petitioner is the person who executed the sale deed of land which was shown to be transferable by the contrivances as stated above.
The donor of the power attorney holder has gone on record to state that she had put her thumb impressions as asked by the other co-accused.

Whether the petitioner had the requisite dishonest intention or not while executing the sale deed is a question of fact that cannot be determined at this stage, and can be decided only after evidence is led on the point.
Materials collected make out a prima facie case against the petitioner.
I am not persuaded by the argument on behalf of the petitioner that no prima facie case is made out.
Criminal miscellaneous petition accordingly stands dismissed.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Jharkhand High Court, Ranchi Dated the 20th July, 2023 AFR /
